Hi Aisha,

Thanks for taking this through with us. BlueMarble is completing vendor setup for Redwood and I attached our onboarding form. A couple of items we need clarified before our finance team will approve the integration:

- PO numbering: do you issue a provisional PO or do we need a purchase-ref first? We need something to attach to our first invoices.
- Spend cap: can we set an annual cap (we expect ~$120k/year) with monthly buckets and alerting?
- Line items: we have two SKUs that may need to be split across cost centers. Is it possible to have a single PO reference with multiple line-item rows (and different spend allocations)?

Attached: blue_marble_onboarding_form.pdf (vendor onboarding form)

Can we get a quick call this week to align and avoid any blocked invoices?

Marta — thanks for the form and the clear list. High level plan: we route initial requests through our Purchase Reference Control Board to ensure PO serialization, spend gating, and any required line-item splits are captured before a PO is issued.

Quick answers up front:
- We can issue a provisional PO number for the ramp so your finance team has something to attach while the purchase-ref is finalized.
- Spend cap enforcement is supported; we typically model it as monthly buckets with automatic alerting at 80%/90% and hard blocks at the monthly cap, configurable per-account.
- Line items: yes — we can map one physical invoice to multiple PO lines with cost-center tagging. Please send the expected monthly spend per SKU and the target cost centers so procurement can split the lines on issuance.

I've looped in Ben (procurement ops) and Laura (vendor onboarding) to coordinate the Control Board review. Attached is our onboarding_checklist.pdf — if you can populate the spend by SKU we can include it in the agenda for tomorrow's 10:30am Control Board slot.

Aisha Rahman
Senior Account Executive, Commercial
Redwood Inference
aisha_rahman@redwood.com

If it's easier, I'm happy to hop on the 10:30 Control Board slot — I see Aisha mentioned tomorrow morning.

Thanks,
Marta
